svg.text: Глава 16 · Протоколы маршрутизации и технология SDN
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0472:c01–p0513:c01 · PDF 472–513 · printed 471–512
1 · Routing control families
Static ↔ dynamic · distributed ↔ centralized
Proactive ↔ reactive · unicast ↔ multicast
DV → distance from neighbors · LS → full topology graph · PV → AS path/policy
Convergence = restore consistent routing state after topology change
Forwarding uses the state produced by the control plane
2 · RIP and OSPF
RIP → periodic neighbor vectors · hop metric · metric 16 unreachable in source
RIP failure mode → stale vectors / count-to-infinity / loops
Mitigation → split horizon · triggered updates · hold-down
OSPF → HELLO → LSA flood → LSDB → Dijkstra/SPF
Areas/ABR/backbone bound the topology database and SPF scope
3 · BGP and routing hierarchy
AS → one administrative routing-policy domain
IGP inside AS · BGP as external gateway protocol between ASes
BGP peers are explicitly configured; source transport = TCP/179
UPDATE → prefix + next hop + AS path; own AS in path → reject loop
iBGP propagation scales from full mesh toward route reflectors
Policy can intentionally prefer a path that is not shortest by a simple metric
4 · Multicast routing
One source copy is replicated only at distribution-tree branches
IGMP → host membership on directly attached subnet
DVMRP / MOSPF / PIM → routing-tree examples in source
Dense → flood/prune · Sparse → explicit join via rendezvous-point concept
RPF validates arrival interface using reverse unicast path toward source
Membership alone is insufficient for end-to-end multicast delivery
5 · SDN / OpenFlow / P4
SDN → separate control logic from packet-forwarding devices
Controller collects state and programs forwarding behavior
OpenFlow rule → match conditions + actions + counters
Table pipeline handles rule scale/processing stages
P4 → program packet-processing architecture, then install runtime rules
6 · NFV / MANO
Network function → software VNF on general-purpose compute
VNF chain → virtual network service
Orchestration → instantiate/connect/manage service functions
MANO → infrastructure manager + VNF manager + orchestrator
SDN controls forwarding; NFV virtualizes functions — complementary, not identical
Operational reading rule
Routing incident → neighbor/session → protocol DB → route selection/policy → installed forwarding state → next hop.
SDN/NFV incident → intended controller/orchestrator state → programmed device/VNF state → counters/health → packet result.
OpenFlow source example contains a TCP-port mismatch; see source-findings.
Chapter 17 starts at p0514:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
